name: q-and-a

escalateTo: split across slides (auto with autosplit: on)
capacity.note: past six Q/A pairs the column overflows a portrait box

density.note: a one-line question and a short answer

split.note: Overflowing Q&A splits as an accent cover → its own native pairs paginated (never flattened). lib/core/carousel.js cover-paginate.

description: Anticipated questions paired with prepared answers — the end-of-pitch 'what we expect to be asked' slide.
purpose: Use to pre-empt the room: line up the three or four hardest questions the audience will raise and answer each one before it is asked. The question reads as a prompt; the prepared answer carries the substance. Distinct from a reference FAQ (many terse look-up pairs) — this is a few weighty defenses of a recommendation.

eyebrow.description: Optional kicker above the headline — wrap a short label in backticks, e.g. `Anticipated questions`.

title.description: Optional headline framing the set — name the pressure ('What the board will press on'), not a bare label ('Q&A').

question.description: One top-level list item per question, in the order you want to take them (lead with the toughest). Author it as plain interrogative text — no bold. Questions are indexed automatically (01, 02, …), so a `ul` and an `ol` render the same.

answer.selector: ul > li > ul > li, ol > li > ol > li
answer.description: The prepared answer, nested one level under its question. Two or three sentences that actually close the question down — a reasoned response, not a restatement. Every question needs one.

skeleton:
<!-- _class: q-and-a -->

## What we expect to be asked.

- First question the audience will raise?
  - The prepared answer — two or three sentences that close it down.
- Second question?
  - The prepared answer.
- Third question?
  - The prepared answer.
sample:
<!-- _class: q-and-a -->

## The Q&A pairs questions with short answers.

- How long may a question run?
  - One line.
- And the answer?
  - Four words or so.
- How many pairs fit?
  - Five; six is the ceiling.
- What if answers run long?
  - Use solo, one per slide.

stressDoc.caption: Six pairs — the hard ceiling.
stressDoc.sample:
<!-- _class: q-and-a compact -->

## Six pairs is the most one slide answers.

- Why six pairs and not seven?
  - The column overflows a portrait box.
- Do answers shrink at the ceiling?
  - To one breath each.
- Where does the eye tire?
  - Pair four; park risk there.
- Can compact buy a seventh?
  - No — six is structural.
- What about longer answers?
  - Fewer pairs, or solo.
- And past six?
  - Autosplit divides the slide.

whenToUse.title: The questions are the point
whenToUse.body: The slide that ends a pitch by naming the hard questions and answering them first. Anticipating the objection and closing it on your terms is more persuasive than waiting to be asked — it signals you have already done the thinking.

whenToUse.title: Three or four weighty pairs
whenToUse.body: A few substantive questions, each with a reasoned two-to-three-sentence answer. Past five the answers compress below persuasion; for a long reference list of one-line look-ups use `faq` or `glossary` instead.

whenToUse.title: Question as prompt, answer as substance
whenToUse.body: The layout deliberately weights the two unequally — the question is the lighter prompt, the answer is the payoff. Lead each pair with the interrogative line and nest the prepared answer one level under it.

antiPatterns.title: A flat FAQ of one-liners
antiPatterns.body: Six or more terse question/answer pairs you flip back to as a reference belong in `faq` or `glossary`, which are built to stack many short look-ups. q-and-a is for a few defended answers, not a help page.

antiPatterns.title: Rhetorical questions with no answer
antiPatterns.body: Every question needs a nested answer that genuinely closes it. A bare question used as a section header or a hook is a `divider` or a `statement`, not a Q&A pair.

antiPatterns.title: Evaluation criteria in disguise
antiPatterns.body: If the top-level item is a requirement you are scoring against (with a rationale below), that is `list-criteria`, not a question you expect to be asked. q-and-a defends; list-criteria evaluates.

## grid deals the pairs into two columns.

- How long may a question run?
  - One line.
- And the answer?
  - Four words or so.
- How many pairs fit?
  - Five; six is the ceiling.
- Why four pairs here?
  - Grids want even counts.

solo.caption: One pair, the whole slide.

## solo gives one question the whole slide.

- What does solo change?
  - One pair, full canvas.

related.name: faq
related.when: many terse reference questions to flip back to, not a few weighty defenses

related.name: glossary
related.when: term/definition reference pairs rather than question/answer pairs

related.name: list-criteria
related.when: numbered criteria with rationale — evaluation, not anticipated objections

related.name: cards-stack
related.when: parallel co-equal cards with no question/answer role split

related.name: decision
related.when: a single verdict to state rather than a set of questions to defend
